content: Oropharyngeal Anthrax Oropharyngeal anthrax is treated with a preferred regimen of Ciprofloxacin 400 mg administered intravenously every 8 hours, combined with either Clindamycin 900 mg IV every 8 hours or Linezolid 600 mg IV every 12 hours. An alternative regimen includes options such as Levofloxacin 750 mg IV every 24 hours, Moxifloxacin 400 mg IV every 24 hours, or other antibiotics like Meropenem, Imipenem, Doripenem, Vancomycin, Ampicillin, or Penicillin G, combined with Doxycycline or Rifampin. Treatment duration is 14 days or until clinical stability is achieved. For patients exposed to aerosolized spores, therapy extends to 60 days, transitioning to oral antibiotics after the first two weeks. Ampicillin and Penicillin G are only suitable for penicillin-susceptible strains. If Vancomycin is used, serum trough levels should be maintained at 15-20 mcg/mL. Doxycycline should be avoided in pregnant or lactating women and children under 8 years of age. Buccal Cellulitis For buccal cellulitis, empiric antimicrobial therapy includes Cefuroxime 50 mg/kg IV every 8 hours, or Cefuroxime 10–15 mg/kg orally every 12 hours (maximum dose: 1 g/day), or Ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg IV every 24 hours. An alternative regimen is Amoxicillin-Clavulanate 90 mg/kg/day orally every 12 hours. If meningitis is suspected, the Cefuroxime dose should be increased to 80 mg/kg IV every 8 hours, or the Ceftriaxone dose to 50 mg/kg IV every 24 hours. Cervico-Facial Actinomycosis The preferred treatment for cervico-facial actinomycosis is Ampicillin 50 mg/kg/day IV every 8 hours for 4-6 weeks, followed by Penicillin V 2-4 g/day orally every 6 hours for 3-6 months. An alternative regimen is Penicillin G 10-20 million units/day IV every 6 hours for 4-6 weeks, followed by Penicillin V 2-4 g/day orally every 6 hours for 3-6 months. For patients allergic to penicillin, Doxycycline, Clindamycin, or Erythromycin may be considered. Deep Neck Infections Community-Acquired Deep Neck Infections Preferred treatment includes Ampicillin-Sulbactam 1.5–3.0 g IV every 6 hours, Clindamycin 600–900 mg IV every 8 hours, or Moxifloxacin 400 mg IV every 24 hours if Eikenella is suspected. Nosocomial Deep Neck Infections or Immunocompromised Hosts Preferred regimens include Ticarcillin-Clavulanate 3 g IV every 6 hours, Piperacillin-Tazobactam 3 g IV every 6 hours, Imipenem-Cilastatin 500 mg IV every 6 hours, Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV every 12 hours, or Levofloxacin 750 mg IV every 24 hours. Deep Neck Infections with High Risk of MRSA Preferred treatment includes Clindamycin 600–900 mg IV every 8 hours or Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole 10 mg/kg/day IV every 8 hours, combined with Vancomycin 1 g IV every 12 hours. Necrotizing Fasciitis The preferred regimen is Ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 8 hours, Clindamycin 600–900 mg IV every 8 hours, and Metronidazole 500 mg IV every 6 hours. Submandibular Space Infections (Including Ludwig Angina) Immunocompetent Hosts Preferred regimens include Penicillin G 2–4 million units IV every 4–6 hours combined with Tobramycin 2 mg/kg IV every 8 hours, Ampicillin-Sulbactam 2 g IV every 4 hours, Clindamycin 600 mg IV every 6 hours, Doxycycline 200 mg IV every 12 hours, Cefoxitin 2 g IV every 6 hours, or Cefotetan 2 g IV every 12 hours. Immunocompromised Hosts Preferred regimens include Cefotaxime 2 g IV every 6 hours, Ceftizoxime 4 g IV every 8 hours, Piperacillin 3 g IV every 4 hours, Imipenem 500 mg IV every 6 hours, Meropenem 1 g IV every 8 hours, or Gatifloxacin 200 mg IV every 24 hours. Lateral Pharyngeal or Retropharyngeal Space Infections Odontogenic Infections For immunocompetent hosts, treatment options include Penicillin G 2–4 million units IV every 4–6 hours combined with Metronidazole 0.5 g IV every 6 hours, Ampicillin-Sulbactam 2 g IV every 4 hours, or Clindamycin 600 mg IV every 6 hours. For immunocompromised hosts, options include Cefotaxime 2 g IV every 6 hours, Ceftizoxime 4 g IV every 8 hours, Piperacillin 3 g IV every 4 hours, Imipenem 500 mg IV every 6 hours, or Gatifloxacin 400 mg IV every 24 hours. Rhinogenic Infections For immunocompetent hosts, treatment options include Penicillin G 2–4 million units IV every 4–6 hours, Ciprofloxacin 200 mg IV every 12 hours combined with Metronidazole 0.5 g IV every 6 hours, Gatifloxacin 400 mg IV every 24 hours, or Clindamycin 600 mg IV every 6 hours. For immunocompromised hosts, the same regimens as odontogenic infections apply. Otogenic Infections For immunocompetent and immunocompromised hosts, the regimens are similar to those for rhinogenic infections. Peritonsillar Abscess (Quinsy) Immunocompetent Hosts Preferred regimens include Penicillin G 2–4 million units IV every 4–6 hours combined with Metronidazole 0.5 g IV every 6 hours, Ampicillin-Sulbactam 2 g IV every 4 hours, Clindamycin 600 mg IV every 6 hours, or Cefoxitin 2 g IV every 6 hours. Immunocompromised Hosts Preferred regimens include Cefotaxime 2 g IV every 6 hours, Ceftizoxime 4 g IV every 8 hours, or Piperacillin 3 g IV every 4 hours. Suppurative Parotitis Immunocompetent Hosts Preferred regimens include Nafcillin 1.5 g IV every 4–6 hours combined with Metronidazole 0.5 g IV every 6 hours, or Clindamycin 600 mg IV every 6 hours. Immunocompromised Hosts Preferred regimens include Vancomycin 0.5 g IV every 6 hours combined with Cefotaxime 2 g IV every 6 hours, Ceftizoxime 4 g IV every 8 hours, or Piperacillin 3 g IV every 4 hours. Malignant Otitis Media Causative Pathogen: Pseudomonas aeruginosa Preferred regimens include Ciprofloxacin 200 mg IV every 12 hours, Tobramycin 2 mg/kg IV every 8 hours combined with Ceftazidime 2 g IV every 6 hours, Piperacillin 3 g IV every 4 hours, or Imipenem 500 mg IV every 6 hours. Facial Erysipelas Preferred treatment is Vancomycin 1 g IV every 12 hours. Alternative options include Daptomycin 4 mg/kg IV every 24 hours or Linezolid 600 mg IV every 12 hours. Mastoiditis Acute Mastoiditis For outpatient treatment, Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg/day orally every 6 hours is preferred if no recent antibiotic use. If antibiotics were used recently, options include Amoxicillin-Clavulanate, Cefdinir, Cefpodoxime, Cefprozil, or Cefuroxime. For inpatient treatment, Cefotaxime 1-2 g IV every 4-8 hours or Ceftriaxone 1 g IV every 24 hours is preferred. Pathogen-directed therapy for MSSA involves Oxacillin 37 mg/kg IV every 6 hours, while MRSA requires Vancomycin 40 mg/kg/day IV every 6-8 hours. Chronic Mastoiditis Empiric therapy includes Imipenem, Piperacillin-Tazobactam, Meropenem, or Ticarcillin-Clavulanate. Treatment is reserved for acute exacerbations or perioperative management. Orbital Cellulitis Preferred treatment includes Vancomycin 1 g IV every 12 hours, Ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 24 hours, and Metronidazole 1 g IV every 12 hours. Alternative regimens involve combinations of Vancomycin, Levofloxacin, Daptomycin, and Metronidazole. Oropharyngeal Candidiasis Preferred treatments include Clotrimazole troches 10 mg topically every 4-5 hours, Nystatin suspension or pastilles topically every 6 hours, or Fluconazole 100–200 mg orally every 24 hours. Alternative regimens include Itraconazole, Posaconazole, Voriconazole, Amphotericin B, or echinocandins like Anidulafungin, Caspofungin, or Micafungin. Otitis Externa Acute Otitis Externa Preferred treatments include topical acetic acid, Ciprofloxacin with Hydrocortisone or Dexamethasone, Neomycin-Polymyxin B-Hydrocortisone, or Ofloxacin for 7-10 days. For fungal otitis externa, Fluconazole is recommended. Chronic Otitis Externa Treatment involves Neomycin-Polymyxin B-Hydrocortisone topically every 6-8 hours and Selenium Sulfide Shampoo. Acute Otitis Media Preferred regimens include Amoxicillin or Amoxicillin-Clavulanate. Alternative options include Cefdinir, Cefuroxime, Cefpodoxime, or Ceftriaxone. For treatment failure, Amoxicillin-Clavulanate or Ceftriaxone is recommended. Parotitis For MSSA, Nafcillin 2 g IV every 4 hours or Oxacillin 2 g IV every 4 hours is preferred. For MRSA, Vancomycin 1 g IV every 12 hours is recommended.
